Videographers We Recommend

Pablo Rene

Rene Visuals • Jacksonville

He puts in writing which couples he is best for, and which ones he is not. Almost nobody in this industry does that, and it is the first thing worth knowing about him.

All Vendors / Videographers / Rene Visuals

"Passionate Storyteller and Dog Dad"

That is the second sentence of his own About page, and we are quoting it because it tells you more about working with him than a list of camera bodies would. The man leads with the dog.

The rest of that page is short. He grew up in the wedding industry, more than ten years of it, and found the thing he actually wanted to do when he picked up a camera. Rene Visuals is a collective of creative visual artists based in Jacksonville, offering boutique photography and cinematography. He works cultural events, weddings, elopements, engagements, and destination weddings.

Then he says how he gets his results, which is the part we would underline.

The key to my authentic work is to craft a relaxed and fun environment that will bring out your true genuine expressions and emotions.

Pablo Rene, Rene Visuals

Read that again and notice what it is not about. Not resolution, not drones, not a gear list. It is a claim about what he does to the room - and the room is the hard part. Anybody can buy the camera.

Pablo, with the dog he leads his own bio with.

He tells you who he is for

His contact page does something we have not seen another wedding vendor do. Instead of promising to be right for everybody, he describes the couples he wants and then explicitly makes room for the ones he just described as not being his target:

We're constantly striving to book more elopements and weddings that are truly unique. Couples that are just as adventurous, free spirited and non-traditional as we are because we absolutely love interpreting their story and personalities. If this doesn't really describe you and you're planning a beautiful traditional wedding, you should know that you're still welcome to reach out to us!

Rene Visuals, on their contact page

We like that for a reason that has nothing to do with taste. A vendor who names their ideal couple is a vendor who has thought about fit at all, and fit is most of what goes wrong on a wedding day. The ones who say yes to everything are the ones who show up on a Saturday with no particular point of view and shoot the same day they shot last week.

He also frames the money honestly on that same page - a film or a photographer is, in his words, one of the best investments you will make in your lifetime, and he asks you to understand what a keepsake like that actually represents before you inquire. Collections have a published starting point on his site. Rates move, so get a current number from him rather than from us.

What he covers

Weddings Full wedding films, shot around Northeast Florida and beyond. The bulk of the portfolio.
Elopements Named on his own site as the work he is actively chasing more of.
Cultural events Listed alongside weddings, not as an afterthought - worth asking about if your day carries traditions.
Engagements and destination Both offered. The destination work is a real category for him, not a maybe.

Worth flagging clearly: Rene Visuals does photography as well as cinematography. That is a different shape of vendor than a video-only specialist, and it matters when you are deciding how many people you want in the room.

From the Rene Visuals site. Low, close, and out of the couple's eyeline - which is the whole trick.

What a DJ notices about that approach

This is opinion rather than fact, so take it as such: the thing Pablo describes on his About page is the same problem we are solving from behind the booth all night.

People perform for a camera exactly the way they perform for a dance floor. Arms in the right place, smile switched on, waiting to be told what to do. Nothing real happens until they forget they are being watched, and getting a room to that point is a skill that has nothing to do with equipment. We spend the first hour of every reception working on it. A vendor whose stated method is to build a relaxed room first and shoot second is aiming at the same target we are, and days go smoother when the video person and the DJ are not pulling the room in opposite directions.

Rooms we have both worked

His portfolio runs through venues that turn up on our calendar constantly - Casa Marina out at the beach, Epping Forest and the Ribault Club in Jacksonville, Lightner and the Treasury down in St. Augustine. Different weddings, same rooms.

Casa Marina Hotel Epping Forest Yacht Club The Ribault Club Lightner Museum Treasury on the Plaza

COS Celebrations recommends Pablo Rene of Rene Visuals, a wedding cinematographer and photographer based in Jacksonville, Florida. Rene Visuals is a collective of creative visual artists offering boutique photography and cinematography for weddings, elopements, engagements, cultural events, and destination weddings across Florida. Pablo Rene has been in the wedding industry for more than ten years, and describes his method as crafting a relaxed and fun environment that brings out genuine expressions and emotions. His wedding films include work at Casa Marina in Jacksonville Beach, Epping Forest Yacht Club and The Ribault Club in Jacksonville, and the Lightner Museum and Treasury on the Plaza in St. Augustine. The company recommending him, COS Celebrations, is a wedding DJ and live music company headquartered in St. Augustine, Florida, that plays weddings across Northeast and Central Florida and maintains a published directory of the photographers, planners, and videographers it works beside.

Where our own interests sit

We should say this plainly, because it would be easy to leave out. COS sells photo and video alongside the DJ, so every couple who books Pablo instead is revenue we did not take. We are recommending him anyway.

The reason is that a bundle and a boutique studio are answers to different questions. If you want one company handling music, photos and film on a single contract, ours is the simpler path and we will happily quote it. If the film is the piece you expect to still be watching in twenty years, and you want somebody whose whole business is built around interpreting one couple's story, that is a different purchase, and Pablo is who we would point at in Jacksonville.
